name: Thornhollow
region_detail: Wooded valley around Alder Run near the western approaches to the northeastern woodlands and the Storbruhn crossing.
site_type: settlement | Inhabited locations | Timber and milling town; administrative seat of the Marquisate of Thornhollow.
history: A woodland trading settlement and timber market developed around sawmills and nearby forest communities before the Edict of the East. Following the war, increased migration and commercial investment expanded the settlement. Elowen Harrowmont selected Thornhollow as the seat of her marquisate in 3E-991.
current_state: In 3E-992 timber concessions, new roads, and expanding mills bring prosperity and conflict. The Forest Office adjudicates competing claims, while the Blackthorns protect commercial routes and enforce the marquessa’s orders. The Velthari and independent woodland communities dispute some concessions; deeper Hollowbough territories remain comparatively isolated.
inhabitants: Lumbermen, carpenters, sawmill workers, merchants, wagoners, settlers, Blackthorns, and visiting woodland peoples including Velthari and Briarhearth residents.
danger_level: Low ordinarily in town; localized industrial hazards and disputes. Conditions on outlying forest roads and logging grounds vary with faction activity.
points_of_interest:
Sawyer’s Row; Millbank and Alder Run; Old Clearing and Split Pine; Harrowmont Hill and Blackthorns headquarters; Camps; Split Stag; Timber Exchange; Forest Office; Morrow’s Mill; Overland Depot; Logger’s Rest; Lantern House; sheriff’s office.

Unresolved elements: Exact map hex; local street plan and building layouts; opening job and rumor selections; the boundaries and progression of disputed timber concessions.
discovery: Wooded valley around Alder Run near the western approaches to the northeastern woodlands and the Storbruhn crossing. Established timber and freight roads link the town with Blackvein, Redvale, Westbridge, and the Great Eastway. Lesser forest trails lead toward logging camps and independent communities.
